content: This medication belongs to the carbapenem class of antibiotics. It is used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. How to Use: Before starting ertapenem, read the Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Review it again each time you receive a refill. This medication is administered via injection, either into a muscle or a vein, as directed by your doctor. It is typically given once or twice daily. If you are using this medication to prevent an infection, it will be administered intravenously by a healthcare professional. For intramuscular injections, follow the manufacturer’s instructions for mixing the medication with a 1% lidocaine solution. If you are administering this medication at home, ensure you have been thoroughly trained by your healthcare provider on how to prepare and use it properly. Before using the medication, visually inspect it for particles or discoloration. Do not use the solution if either is present. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. To achieve the best results, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue using it for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Side Effects: Common side effects include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site. Other possible side effects include upset stomach, headache, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition known as Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea. This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not a complete list of potential side effects. If you are in the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Precautions: Before using ertapenem, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other carbapenems (e.g., imipenem), penicillins, cephalosporins, or any other substances. If you are receiving an intramuscular injection, also inform your doctor if you are allergic to amide-type local anesthetics (e.g., lidocaine). This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Ertapenem may interfere with live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine), reducing their effectiveness. This medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Notes: While using this medication, your doctor may order lab tests (e.g., complete blood count, kidney function tests) to monitor your progress. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: It is important to receive each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Storage: Consult the product instructions or your pharmacist for storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
